title: SLO-anchored alert chorus and cost inspector prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable ‘alert chorus’ that groups related alerts around SLO anchors and surfaces an inline ‘cost inspector’ showing estimated per-alert and per-incident token/cost impact. This should help on-call engineers prioritize SLO-risking alerts that have high operational or billing impact, and provide one-click links to the postmortem and escalation flows.

Context: Customers use Redwood Console to monitor SLOs, alerts and incidents. Current alert cards are siloed; responders lack quick cost context and fast access to postmortem artifacts or the current on-call owner. We want a prototype that: groups alerts by SLO trajectory, provides a lightweight timeline strip anchored to the SLO window, and shows a cost breakdown that maps alert activity to token/compute cost estimates (hosted / dedicated / private variants).

Key features in prototype:
- Alert chorus grouping: visually clusters alerts that affect the same SLO (color-coded by severity + SLO delta).
- SLO-anchor timeline: a horizontal micro-timeline for each group showing SLO burn and recent alert spikes. Clicking the anchor expands a focused timeline view.
- Cost inspector: a hover/expand control that shows 1) estimated tokens/sec triggered by this alert, 2) estimated hourly compute cost, 3) suggested mitigations (e.g., lower model temp, route to cheaper model variant, apply prefix caching), and 4) historical cost delta when similar alerts occurred.
- On-call baton: compact owner chip with a one-click transfer flow and a ‘notify current owner’ quick action.
- Postmortem & incident links: direct link to a draft postmortem template in Drive and a link to the incident thread; when no postmortem exists, prompt to create one from a templated PRD.
- Accessibility: ensure color contrast on SLO deltas, keyboard navigable timeline, and aria labels for cost inspector components.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Density vs. clarity: chorus groups reduce vertical noise but risk hiding low-frequency alerts; we expose a ‘show all’ toggle per group.
- Cost estimation accuracy: show an explicit confidence band and a link to the cost model used (how estimates are calculated).
- Cross-product scope: cost inspector surface references billing models (hosted/dedicated/private) which may require PM/finance input; prototype will use placeholder rate tables.

Deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop + narrow sidebar view), annotated handoff doc, microcopy for cost inspector states, and a short usability script for 5 participant tests.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates grouping behavior for alerts across 3 SLO scenarios (regression, steady drift, transient spike)
Cost inspector shows token estimate, hourly compute estimate, and mitigation suggestions with confidence band copy
One-click owner notify and transfer flows are wireframed and can be demoed end-to-end
Prototype includes accessible keyboard interactions and aria annotations documented in the handoff doc
Design handoff includes clear links to data inputs required for engineering (rate table, SLO mapping logic)
